classification.difficultyReason: Find an acute angle from an exact ratio or inverse sine, then supply its obtuse supplement. For negative cosine, identify the corresponding obtuse angle using the taught sign relationship.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the acute and the obtuse angle whose sine is $\frac{1}{2}$.

answer.worked:
The acute angle is $30^\circ$ because $\sin 30^\circ=\frac{1}{2}$. Supplementary angles have the same sine.
$$\begin{aligned}\theta_{\text{obtuse}}&=180^\circ-30^\circ\\\theta_{\text{obtuse}}&=150^\circ\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find, correct to the nearest degree, two angles whose sine is approximately $0.5738$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha&=\sin^{-1}(0.5738)\\\alpha&\approx35.0156^\circ\\\beta&=180^\circ-\alpha\\\beta&\approx144.9844^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Supplementary angles have the same sine, so the angles are $35^\circ$ and $145^\circ$, correct to the nearest degree.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find, correct to the nearest degree, an angle whose cosine is approximately $-0.8746$.

answer.worked:
Use $\cos\theta=-\cos(180^\circ-\theta)$.
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha&=\cos^{-1}(0.8746)\\\alpha&\approx29.0023^\circ\\\theta&=180^\circ-\alpha\\\theta&\approx151^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The angle is $151^\circ$, correct to the nearest degree.
